thread.title_full: Questioning of potential jurors in starvation trial to resume Monday - NewsBreak

author: Doris Maricle
title: Questioning of potential jurors in starvation trial to resume Monday - NewsBreak
text:
By Doris Maricle ,
16 hours ago Jury selection remains incomplete in the murder trial of a Lake Arthur couple charged in the 2022 death of their adopted son more than three years ago.
By the end of the third day of jury selection Wednesday, attorneys had selected 11 of 14 potential jurors from a field of 70 people.
Twelve jurors and two alternates are needed in the trial of Adam Duhon, 46, and Jennifer Duhon, 45. The couple is accused in the death of their 12-year-old adopted son, Brogan Nash, who died from complications of malnutrition.
Because the panel was not completed, Judge Steve Gunnell ordered that more than 75 additional prospective jurors be personally served and report to court at 9 a.m. Monday, when jury selection is scheduled to resume.
“We don’t have 12 members and we have to get a new panel served and ordered back to court on Monday,” Gunnell said.
Before dismissing the remaining prospective jurors for the weekend, Gunnell instructed them to avoid any information related to the case, including posts on social media.
“If you see something ignore it if you can,” he told potential jurors.
He also directed prospective jurors not to search online for information about the case.
Jurors are required to decide the case based only on evidence and testimony presented in court, but Gunnell noted that discussions on social media has made it more difficult to find an impartial jury,
During questioning this week, several prospective jurors said they had heard about the case through social media, news reports or conversations with others.
The court is expected to continue questioning the new prospective jurors Monday in an effort to complete the panel before opening statements begin.
The trial is expected to last two to three weeks.
